key_insight: SpecGP is a transformer-based model that predicts collision-energy–adaptable structural MS/MS spectra for N‑glycopeptides, increasing fragment ion coverage to improve isomer discrimination and boost identification confidence via rescoring.
problem_solved: Existing spectral prediction approaches struggle to model fragment patterns across different collision energies for glycopeptides, limiting fragment coverage, reducing isomer separation power, and lowering identification confidence.
method: Transformer-based architecture that conditions spectral predictions on collision energy to produce energy-adaptable spectra for N‑glycopeptides.
Learns and enhances fragment ion coverage by modeling structural fragmentation patterns specific to glycopeptide motifs and energies.
Integrates predicted spectra into a rescoring pipeline to improve isomer discrimination and final identification confidence.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a transferable, energy-conditioned spectral prediction approach that improves downstream proteomics identification and demonstrates transformer effectiveness for structured spectral modeling in glycoproteomics.
visual_elements: Schematic of SpecGP transformer with an explicit collision-energy input node (architecture diagram).
Overlay spectra plots showing predicted vs experimental MS/MS at multiple collision energies, highlighting increased fragment coverage.
Before/after comparison charts (precision/recall or ROC) showing improved isomer discrimination and identification scores after rescoring.
End-to-end pipeline flowchart: raw MS → SpecGP prediction → rescoring → improved identifications (icons for instrument, model, and results).
paper_title: SpecGP as a transformer-based model for predicting energy-adaptable structural spectra of glycopeptides
paper_authors: Xianyong Wang, Rui Song, Zhuangzhuang Feng, Shisheng Sun
